summary: Ian Smith, Rhodesian-born prime minister of Rhodesia from 1964, illegally declared independence from Britain in 1965 to preserve white minority rule and waged the brutal Bush War until 1979.

evidence.note: Story of Rhodesia begins with the 1889 royal charter to the British South Africa Company
Hut tax and pass laws built to force black Africans into labour for white farms and mines
Smith born 1919 in Selukwe to a settler family
Smith and Winston Field found the Rhodesian Front, which wins the 1962 election
Smith becomes prime minister in 1964; host argues he ruled as a de facto dictator
Host frames the Bush War as an internal civil war for black emancipation, not a Cold War proxy
Extended segment on the Selous Scouts pseudo-operations and turned prisoners
Chemical and biological warfare: poisoned wells, anthrax, human trials on prisoners
Raids into Mozambique, including Operation Eland; later invasions of Zambia and Mozambique
Recruitment of foreign white supremacists and far-right support networks abroad
Smith's retirement in Zimbabwe and death in Cape Town in 2007

notes: covered_span starts at 1889 because Part 1 spends a long segment on the BSAC founding of Rhodesia, the 1890s wars and early labour laws; a reviewer may treat this as background and start at 1919. Transcript says 'Universal Declaration of Independence'; the actual name is Unilateral. Primary theme could also be racism-white-supremacy.
